"""Headline title casing for article and newsletter titles."""

SMALL_WORDS = frozenset({
    "a", "an", "and", "as", "at", "but", "by", "for", "in", "nor",
    "of", "on", "or", "per", "the", "to", "via",
})

_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION = ".,:;!?"


def title_case(text: str) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` in headline title case.

    ``text`` is split on single spaces into words. Each word is converted on
    its own and the words are joined again with single spaces:

    1. A word with an uppercase letter anywhere after its first character
       (such as "iPhone", "NASA" or "McKinsey") is kept exactly as written.
    2. Otherwise, if the word with any trailing ``.,:;!?`` characters removed
       is, in lowercase, one of ``SMALL_WORDS`` (a, an, and, as, at, but, by,
       for, in, nor, of, on, or, per, the, to, via), the word is written in
       lowercase -- unless it is the first or the last word of ``text``, in
       which case its first character is uppercased.
    3. Every other word has its first character uppercased.
    """
    words = text.split(" ")
    result = []
    for index, word in enumerate(words):
        if index > 0 and word.rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION).lower() in SMALL_WORDS:
            result.append(word.lower())
        else:
            result.append(word.capitalize())
    return " ".join(result)

"""Headline title casing for article and newsletter titles."""

SMALL_WORDS = frozenset({
    "a", "an", "and", "as", "at", "but", "by", "for", "in", "nor",
    "of", "on", "or", "per", "the", "to", "via",
})

_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION = ".,:;!?"


def _has_interior_uppercase(word: str) -> bool:
    """Return ``True`` if ``word`` has an uppercase letter after position 0."""
    return any(char.isupper() for char in word[1:])


def title_case(text: str) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` in headline title case.

    ``text`` is split on single spaces into words. Each word is converted on
    its own and the words are joined again with single spaces:

    1. A word with an uppercase letter anywhere after its first character
       (such as "iPhone", "NASA" or "McKinsey") is kept exactly as written.
    2. Otherwise, if the word with any trailing ``.,:;!?`` characters removed
       is, in lowercase, one of ``SMALL_WORDS`` (a, an, and, as, at, but, by,
       for, in, nor, of, on, or, per, the, to, via), the word is written in
       lowercase -- unless it is the first or the last word of ``text``, in
       which case its first character is uppercased.
    3. Every other word normally has its first character uppercased, with one
       exception: within a clause (the run of words since the start of
       ``text`` or since the previous word ending in trailing punctuation),
       once a *second* small word has appeared, the word immediately
       following that second small word is written in lowercase instead --
       unless it is the first or the last word of ``text``. Later words in
       the clause go back to being capitalised normally.
    """
    words = text.split(" ")
    last_index = len(words) - 1
    result = []
    small_word_streak = 0
    lower_next = False
    for index, word in enumerate(words):
        is_edge = index == 0 or index == last_index
        core = word.rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION)

        if _has_interior_uppercase(word):
            result.append(word)
            lower_next = False
        elif not is_edge and core.lower() in SMALL_WORDS:
            result.append(word.lower())
            small_word_streak += 1
            lower_next = small_word_streak >= 2
        else:
            if lower_next and not is_edge:
                result.append(word.lower())
            else:
                result.append(word.capitalize())
            lower_next = False

        if core != word:
            small_word_streak = 0

    return " ".join(result)
